en.stage1Journal: Nearest 10: When we round to the nearest 10, we look at the ones digit. If it is 0 to 4, we round down to the lower multiple of 10. If it is 5 to 9, we round up to the next multiple of 10.
en.stage1Task1: Examine the items on the work benches
en.stage1Task2: Choose something made of matter that will dissolve in water
en.stage1Task3: Inflate the balloon with the button
en.stage1Text2: Today we are going to perform experiments to determine what makes up matter
en.stage1Text3: Let's move into the next room. You can move around with the WASD keys or the arrow keys.
en.stage1Text4: Here we are in the lab! Let’s investigate matter.
en.stage1Text5: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. The amount of space it takes up is called its volume.
en.stage1Text6: All the substances around us are made of matter, even the air we breathe!
en.stage1Text7: There are 5 items on the workbenches. Let’s examine each one and discover which are matter. Walk up to a bench to take a closer look.
en.stage1Text8: On this table is a patch of light from a lamp. Select it to take a closer look or click the cross to leave the table.
en.stage1Text9: Use the button to switch the lamp on and off. Observe what happens to the patch of light. Does anything physical get added to or removed from the table?
en.stage1Text10: Think about what you just observed and what you know about matter. Select the statements that correctly describe the mass and volume of light.
en.stage1Text11: Well done! Light is a form of energy, not matter. It has no mass and does not occupy space in the same way that matter does.
en.stage1Text12: Something is not correct. Try again or come back to this object later.
en.stage1Text13: On this table is an object casting a shadow. Select the shadow to take a closer look or click the cross to leave the table.
en.stage1Text14: Use the button to switch the light source on and off. Observe what happens to the shadow. Does the object casting the shadow change in any way?
en.stage1Text15: Think about what you just observed and what you know about matter. Select the statements that correctly describe the mass and volume of a shadow.
en.stage1Text16: Well done! A shadow forms when an object blocks light. A shadow is not matter because it has neither mass nor volume.
en.stage1Text18: This is the shadow cast by the cube. The cube blocks some of the light from the light source, so less light reaches this part of the table. The shadow shows where the light is blocked. The cube has mass and takes up space, but the shadow itself has no mass.
en.stage1Text19: Select all correct statements about the mass and volume of this shadow.
en.stage1Text20: On this table are some sugar cubes. Select them to take a closer look.
en.stage1Text21: Sugar cubes are made of tiny sugar crystals pressed together. When sugar dissolves in water, its particles spread throughout the water. The sugar is still there, even though its particles are too small to see.
en.stage1Text22: Select all correct statements about the mass and volume of sugar.
en.stage1Text23: Oh look, a tank of water has appeared inside the lab. Let's go look at it.

es.stage1Text11: On this table are a ceramic cup filled with water. Click the item to learn about its properties. Click the cross to leave the table.
es.stage1Text12: This ceramic cup contains two states of matter. The cup itself is a solid, while the water inside is a liquid. The cup keeps its shape, but the water takes the shape of its container.

es.stage1Text14: On this table is a balloon filled with air. Click the balloon to explore its properties. Click the cross to leave the table.
es.stage1Text15: The balloon is made of stretchy rubber and contains air, a mixture of gases. As more air enters the balloon, the rubber stretches and the balloon grows larger.

es.stage1Text17: This block is casting a shadow, lets click the shadow itself and take a closer look.
